QQQE holds the same 100 NASDAQ stocks as QQQ but caps each position near 1%, slashing concentration risk for retirees.

QQQ holds about 8 times more NVIDIA per dollar than QQQE, and Apple shows a similar 6-to-1 gap between the two funds.

QQQE beat QQQ over the past year (15% vs. 13%) but badly trailed over 10 years (296% vs. 511%).

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Apple didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat AAPL. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Most people who buy Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) want broad exposure to the NASDAQ-100. That portfolio leans heavily on a few chipmakers and tech platforms. Retirees and near-retirees who like the growth of those 100 companies but don't want so much riding on a few of them can look at a smaller fund. It holds the same holdings on very different terms: the Direxion NASDAQ-100 Equal Weighted Index ETF (NASDAQ:QQQE).

Spencer Platt / Getty Images
NVIDIA Holds 7.6% of QQQ but Under 1% of QQQE

QQQ seeks to track the investment results, before fees and expenses, of the Nasdaq-100 Index, and it weights each company by market value. As of June 30, 2026, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) was its largest holding at 7.60% of net assets. QQQE owns the same company, but as of July 31, 2026, NVIDIA made up only 0.97% of the fund. Using those two filing dates, QQQ held about 7.8 times as much NVIDIA per dollar invested.

------

Free Report, Just Released

Why Didn't AAPL Make The Top 10 List?

24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.

And AAPL didn't make the cut!

The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.

Enter Your Email and See the Ten →

------

The same pattern holds. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) was 6.67% of QQQ as of June 30, compared with 1.01% of QQQE as of July 31. That's a ratio of roughly 6.6 to 1. The two filings are a month apart, so the weights have moved since then. The gap itself is built in, though. QQQE regularly rebalances every holding back to a roughly equal piece, while QQQ lets its biggest winners keep growing.

Six Giants Take Up a Third of QQQ

In QQQ's June 30 filing, its six largest holdings, led by NVIDIA and Apple, added up to about 32.4% of the fund. In QQQE's July 31 filing, those same six names came to roughly 5.9%. QQQE's equity weights ran from 0.4425047962% to 1.3017191224%, and most positions sat near 1%. The money that QQQ puts into its giants is spread across health care, industrials, utilities, consumer and software companies. In QQQ, those companies get much smaller slices.

A $1.33 Billion Fund Next to a $490 Billion Giant

QQQE reported $1.33 billion in net assets as of July 31, 2026. QQQ reported $490.1 billion as of June 30, which makes it roughly 368 times larger. Trading volume shows the same gap. On October 29, 154,014 QQQE shares changed hands, compared with 37,532,845 for QQQ. QQQ's long track record keeps it in the spotlight.

QQQE's figures are adjusted for distributions, while QQQ's reflect price changes only. That means the table actually understates QQQ's long-term advantage. Over the past year and so far in 2026, QQQE has come out ahead. Over the most recent month, it fell less than QQQ did.

Know the Trade-Offs of Equal Weighting

Equal weighting falls behind when the biggest companies lead the market. Our May 20 analysis indicated that QQQ's concentration was beating equal weight during the AI spending cycle, and the five- and 10-year figures support that view. Because QQQE keeps each winner near 1%, it gets less of any mega-cap rally. The same rebalancing also means more trading inside the fund.

QQQE's smaller size and lower trading can mean wider bid-ask spreads, so it's worth checking quotes before placing an order. A fund with modest assets also faces more risk of being closed than a giant does. If assets shrink, the sponsor can shut down the fund, forcing shareholders into a sale, and possibly a tax bill, on someone else's schedule. At $1.33 billion, QQQE is well established, but it's small next to its rival. Cost belongs in the comparison too. QQQ's prospectus lists a management fee of 0.18%, so look up QQQE's current expense ratio in Direxion's fund documents before deciding.

Who QQQE Suits, and Who Is Better Off With QQQ

QQQE suits investors who are nervous about how much of QQQ depends on a few names. That includes retirees who don't want one chipmaker's earnings report to swing a large part of their savings. QQQ lines up more closely with investors who expect the largest NASDAQ companies to keep leading and who value deep liquidity and a huge asset base. Both funds own the same companies. The key difference is how much of your money sits in the top few. QQQE's next portfolio filing will show how far its equal slices shifted during the fall.

October has been anything but smooth for Wall Street, as the tech-heavy focus on big U.S. indexes has hit the stock market. Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ETF Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 QQQ has lost about 3.3%. The key issue is that investors are increasingly questioning whether the massive spending on AI will generate enough profits to justify current valuations. 

AI's Cursed October

The tech sector and AI trade have struggled in October. The month saw AI-driven vulnerabilities that led to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents, a trend dubbed "Black October." The term refers to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents in October 2026 that were accelerated by AI. 

Meanwhile, the AI debt boom remains a key concern. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.3% at the start of the month, reviving concerns about borrowing costs and the massive debt financing used to build AI data centers.  

Investors have been constantly reassessing technology valuations amid rising rates and heavy corporate borrowing. Roundhill Generative AI & Technology ETF CHAT is off 12.6% over the past month (as of Oct. 29, 2026) 

Cybersecurity: The AI Winner of October 

AI is introducing new cybersecurity threats while creating significant long-term growth opportunities for cybersecurity companies and ETFs. Following the Hugging Face incident, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta have all reported instances of AI agents escaping test sandboxes and accessing external systems. 

Meanwhile, cybercriminals are leveraging AI to execute increasingly sophisticated attacks, making cybersecurity spending a business necessity rather than a discretionary expense. 

State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF XLK is off more than 3% over the past month (as of Oct. 29, 2026), whileWisdomTree Cybersecurity Fund (WCBR) has surged about 10.3% during the same timeframe. 

Alphabet's Plunge After Earnings: Cash Generation Is Now an Issue

Alphabet GOOGL plunged about 13% Thursday (at the time of writing) after its third-quarter results, putting it on track for its worst day since going public in 2004, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.  

The stock lost about $524 billion in market value at its low, the second-largest one-day loss for a U.S.-listed company after NVIDIA's $593 billion wipeout in January 2025 (the day China's DeepSeek's cheaper AI model claims upset AI investors).

Shares of Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) fell 11.47% in Friday's session to $142.17 as of 9:45 AM ET. That continues a slide that has the stock down 25.18% over the past month and 37.13% year to date. For ETF holders, the drop reaches every fund that owns the stock, and in some crypto-equity funds Coinbase is one of the biggest positions.

24/7 Wall St.

Two Same-Day Hits Sent Coinbase Lower

Coinbase did not issue a press release on Friday. Same-day headlines pointed to a selloff across crypto stocks after Binance froze assets following a reported $6.3 billion heist, according to a post from the markets news account DeItaone on X. Barron's added that crypto investors should still worry even though U.S.-listed crypto names are separate from Binance.

The heist news landed on top of a mixed earnings report released Thursday after the close. Coinbase posted GAAP diluted EPS of $2.51, beating a $0.07 consensus, but $715.0 million of gains on crypto assets held for investment did much of the work. Adjusted net income was only $77.7 million. Revenue of $1.22 billion came in just short of expectations and fell 35.0% year over year. On the earnings call, the company's chief financial officer, Alesia Haas, said overall crypto spot trading volume fell 10% quarter over quarter, with growth in prediction markets making up for the decline.

Analysts lowered their targets on Friday. Barclays cut its target to $120 from $149, Wells Fargo cut to $174 from $200 and Jefferies cut to $174 from $183.

COIN Analyst Ratings — 24/7 Wall St.
Crypto-Equity Funds Carry the Heaviest Exposure

Coinbase makes up the largest share of the Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (NYSEARCA:BITQ). It was the fund's biggest holding at 9.998% of net assets as of June 30, 2026. If that weight still holds, today's move alone takes about 1.15 percentage points off the fund. Most of BITQ's other top holdings are bitcoin miners and crypto treasury companies that usually trade on the same news.

The ARK Innovation ETF (NYSEARCA:ARKK) held a $231.8 million Coinbase stake, or 4.17% of net assets, as of July 31, 2026. ARKK fell 4.91% to $81.75 early Friday. Coinbase accounts for only about 0.48 percentage points of that drop, which shows how much the fund's other stablecoin, brokerage and crypto-platform holdings fell alongside it.

The Amplify Transformational Data Sharing ETF (NYSEARCA:BLOK) held Coinbase at 2.28% of net assets as of June 30. It still fell 5.72% to $51.56, because its other holdings (miners, exchanges and trading apps) are just as sensitive to crypto sentiment.

In thematic funds, concentration builds on itself. When the largest holding and the next ten positions all react to the same crypto headlines, a fund's day can look a lot like the sector's worst day.

Index Fund Holders Face Smaller but Real Overlap Risk

The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) held no Coinbase shares as of June 30, 2026. Its index covers the largest non-financial companies listed on NASDAQ exchanges, and Coinbase is classified in financial services.

Broad-market funds do own Coinbase, which joined the S&P 500 in 2025, so S&P 500 trackers, total-market funds and many target-date funds hold it. With a market value of about $31.68 billion, its weight in those funds is small, and a day like Friday barely moves them.

Overlap is where retirement savers can get caught. An IRA that pairs an S&P 500 core with ARKK or BITQ as a growth satellite owns Coinbase several times over, plus a collection of stocks that move with crypto. Comparing each fund's holdings against the others shows the part of the portfolio tied to one theme.

Q4 Guidance and Fund Filings Come Next

For the fourth quarter, Coinbase reported quarter-to-date transaction revenue of about $165 million through October 25 and guided subscription and services revenue to $550 million to $630 million. Management warned that trading volume could swing in the near term as it finishes integrating Deribit and INTX. Coinbase still has $2.0 billion left on its buyback authorization. The next round of fund holdings disclosures will show whether managers trimmed Coinbase or added more during the slide.
